title: When Sample-Splitting Choices Matter in TMLE and AIPW: Cross-Fitting, Targeting, and Repetition
abstract: arXiv:2610.16192v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Variants of targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) and augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with machine-learning nuisance models differ in which observations train them, how bias is corrected, and whether splits are repeated. In known-truth simulations of a binary-outcome average treatment effect, eight headline estimators shared each setting's library, inner folds and truncation bound; coverage differences were judged against a prespecified two-percentage-point margin. With a low-complexity library and good overlap (n = 3000), all but a half-sample baseline covered equivalently (0.928-0.939). With one random forest on the primary data-generating mechanism, estimators fitting the propensity in-sample undercovered severely (0.12-0.48), whereas cross-fitting both nuisances raised coverage to 0.91-1.00, two overcovering. Under near-positivity, every AIPW estimator covered better than every TMLE estimator with the unweigh

translated_title: TMLE与AIPW中样本拆分选择何时重要：交叉拟合、靶向估计与重复拆分
translated_abstract: 采用机器学习干扰模型的靶向最大似然估计（TMLE）和增强逆概率加权（AIPW）的各种变体在以下方面存在差异：使用哪些观测数据训练模型、如何校正偏差，以及是否重复数据拆分。在二元结局平均处理效应的已知真值模拟中，八种主要估计器共享每个设置下的学习器库、内部折数和截断界限；覆盖率差异依据预先设定的两个百分点容差进行评判。在低复杂度学习器库和良好协变量重叠（n = 3000）的条件下，除半样本基线外，所有估计器的覆盖率表现等价（0.928–0.939）。当在主数据生成机制上仅使用一个随机森林时，在样本内拟合倾向得分的估计器出现严重覆盖不足（0.12–0.48），而对两个干扰模型均进行交叉拟合则将覆盖率提升至0.91–1.00（其中两个出现过度覆盖）。在近正性（near-positivity）违规条件下，每种AIPW估计器的覆盖率均优于每种TMLE估计器，而未加权……
tldr: 该研究通过已知真值模拟系统比较了八种TMLE和AIPW估计器变体，发现对两个干扰模型均进行交叉拟合是实现有效置信区间覆盖率的关键（样本内拟合倾向得分会导致严重覆盖不足），且在近正性违规条件下AIPW估计器的覆盖率表现一致优于TMLE估计器。
en_tdlr: Through known-truth simulations comparing eight TMLE and AIPW estimator variants, this study shows that cross-fitting both nuisance models is essential for valid confidence interval coverage (in-sample propensity fitting causes severe undercoverage), and that AIPW estimators consistently achieve better coverage than TMLE estimators under near-positivity violations.
